correctness.rationale: Explicit total transition maps realize each of the three claimed state budgets. If a k-state DFA lies below them, all cycle lengths <=k divide marker displacement and the trailing suffix has length >=k-1. Nonmaximal zero-letter orbit transient gives the same marker input state; maximal transient forces f^(k-1) constant, so no lower-size separator exists. Includes boundary and k=1 cases. Attached checker independently corroborates 274 full-map and 9231 all-zero-map finite inputs and n up to 200 thresholds.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Robson provides general asymptotic separability; Demaine et al. provide general O(log n) for a single differing run and marker-padding lower examples; Nicol strengthens parameterized general upper bounds. Their statements, while broader in word class, do not determine the exact minimum for every choice of n,i,j and so do not subsume the equality.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The 2011 left and right boundary constructions prove only two upper bounds, and its lcm examples establish lower bounds for selected high-padding instances. The new lower bound for all i,j requires an exhaustive orbit-transient argument, including maximal transient forcing a global sink, and therefore does not follow from the cited general asymptotic or endpoint inequalities. Nicol’s later runs-of-differences bound similarly does not give exact cases.

value.rationale: Resolves a classical finite-automaton distinguishing-size problem exactly for every pair of equal-length binary words with one marked bit, differentiating three structural regimes. Produces sharp arithmetic threshold for when k states are necessary in this class, and a mathematically motivated asymptotic sequence; not a routine finite enumeration or a bare corollary of an unrestricted bound.
